newsitem.title: USA: Wyeth-Ayerst working on fen/phen box label.
newsitem.headline: Wyeth-Ayerst working on fen/phen box label.

text.p: Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories, a unit of American Home Products Corp, said Friday that it is working with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to develop appropriate warning language about potential serious side effects of concomitant use of fenfluramine and phentermine ("fen/phen").
Wyeth-Ayerst said that when the language is finalized, a warning will be boxed in the physician and patient labeling of the company's antiobesity products.

The company said that the revised labeling for Pondimin (fenfluramine hydrochloride) tablets C-IV will include a boxed warning about a possible serious heart valve disorder which has been reported with concomitant use of "fen/phen".

Revised labeling including a boxed warning for Redux (dexfenfluramine hydrochloride capsules) C-IV, which is marketed in the U.S. by Wyeth-Ayerst, has also been submitted to the FDA because it is a related chemical compound to fenfluramine.
A boxed warning is the method used in product labeling to prominently display information on special problems of a critical nature.
